summary:
The biggest event today (Nov 9) is a regulatory one. The FDA has required a NAION warning (sudden, painless vision loss in one eye) on the labels of every approved GLP-1 medicine, including Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo. I confirmed this on the FDA Drug Safety Communication. In a meta-analysis of 126 trials, NAION occurred at 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years (GLP-1 vs comparators). A real-world study (Sentinel) found 30–32 per 100,000 person-years and a hazard ratio of 1.43 vs DPP-4 inhibitors. Google Trends shows 1000+ searches, and CNN, Reuters, WSJ, NBC, STAT and the FT all covered it within hours. Most existing creator videos still frame this as a semaglutide-only 'Ozempic blindness' story. That leaves an opening for a calm, tirzepatide-first 'vision changes: what's normal and what's urgent' piece. It fits Lane A. Search interest should peak over the next 3–7 days.

Second: Lilly's ATTAIN-OSA Phase 3 trial of the orforglipron pill (Foundayo) for sleep apnea was published in JAMA and presented at AHA today. Apnea events per hour fell by 21.1 vs 4.3 on placebo without PAP, and 18.3 vs 5.5 with PAP. Lilly plans to file with the FDA by the end of 2026. This suits a 13:00 lead Short with tirzepatide named first (tirzepatide is already approved for sleep apnea).

Carry-overs keep accelerating: Thanksgiving (seen 10 times, peak Nov 18–27), injection site reactions, sick-day dehydration, and alcohol, which a new target trial emulation (an observational study designed to mimic a trial) has refreshed. Prep ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) for REDEFINE 4. It's a randomized CagriSema vs tirzepatide head-to-head, which is the playbook's only allowed news exception.

Rejected: compounded or online 'where to buy' content and 'natural GLP-1' supplement roundups.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and sudden vision loss: the FDA's new NAION warning for all GLP-1 medicines (Nov 9, 2026)
candidates.angle: Calm, tirzepatide-first 'Is this normal?' explainer. Blurry vision from blood-sugar shifts is common and usually temporary. NAION is different: rare, sudden, painless, one eye, often noticed on waking. Explain why that one needs a same-day call. Give the FDA numbers with the right units: 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years across 126 trials, and a hazard ratio of 1.43 vs DPP-4 inhibitors in Sentinel. The risk appears higher in people who've had NAION before. Scope the label wording: the prescriber decides about continuing if NAION happens. Don't stop on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
keywords: is blurry vision normal on tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–6 days (news spike today, creator wave and search peak this week)
candidates.why_now: The FDA Drug Safety Communication went out today. It requires a NAION warning on every approved GLP-1, and it's the first US class-wide label change to include tirzepatide. Google Trends shows 1000+ searches, and more than 15 mainstream outlets covered it within hours. Existing videos frame it as a semaglutide 'Ozempic blindness' story from 2024–25, so tirzepatide-specific, label-accurate content is still thin.

evidence.signal: Class-wide NAION warning (Warnings and Precautions). 126-trial meta-analysis: 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years. Sentinel: HR 1.43 vs DPP-4 inhibitors
FDA warns GLP-1 drugs carry potential risk of rare eye condition
FDA requires NAION warning across the GLP-1 class

candidates.topic: The orforglipron pill (Foundayo) for sleep apnea: ATTAIN-OSA Phase 3 in JAMA, and how it compares with tirzepatide (already approved for OSA)
candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short with tirzepatide named first: 'Tirzepatide is already approved for sleep apnea. Now a daily GLP-1 pill has Phase 3 data.' Numbers are adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA over 52 weeks. Without PAP: −21.1 vs −4.3 events per hour (placebo). With PAP: −18.3 vs −5.5. Stopped due to side effects: 12.2% vs 3.8% (Study 1) and 6.8% vs 0.6% (Study 2). Not yet approved for OSA; Lilly plans to file by the end of 2026. These are separate trials from SURMOUNT-OSA, not head-to-head.
candidates.why_now: Presented at AHA 2026 and published in JAMA today, with STAT and Scientific American coverage. Health creators haven't covered it yet. It fits the playbook's 'fresh randomized result' lead slot.

evidence.signal: ATTAIN-OSA: 2 studies, n=363 and n=349, 52 weeks, AHI results vs placebo, submission by end of 2026
Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Results From 2 Randomized Clinical Trials
Foundayo helped alleviate sleep apnea in studies

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: redness, itching, small lumps. What the label reports per dose and when to call
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, ranked #1 in the playbook. Calm 'Is this normal?' framing. Give label rates per dose: 6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 and 15 mg, vs about 2% on placebo. Cover rotating sites and what fades on its own, then infection and allergy red flags. Serious allergic reactions are post-marketing reports: stop and get medical help right away. Then the scoped don't-stop line.
candidates.why_now: Its Short reached 226 views by day 3. Momentum rose in 10 snapshots (73→88). No live video on the channel answers it, and it's the first new Lane A topic in the playbook.

candidates.topic: Sick days on tirzepatide: cold, flu or stomach bug, dehydration signs and the label's kidney warning
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide Dehydration: Signs to Watch For'. Winter-illness framing for the US, UK and Canada, plus summer heat for Australia. The label links acute kidney injury to dehydration from vomiting or diarrhoea. Cover the signs, when to call, and asking a pharmacist about cold medicines. No dosing or skip-dose advice; say 'ask your prescriber about a sick-day plan'.
candidates.why_now: Several related snapshots at 72–80. Ranked #2 for Lane A in the playbook, and seasonal illness is ramping up now. Pairs naturally with the 11-09 diarrhoea long-form via watch-next linking.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol: what the label and new research say (JAMA Psychiatry survey plus the Nov 3 target trial emulation of semaglutide, tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide and Alcohol: What to Know'. Survey: 44.2% of drinkers on GLP-1s reported drinking less (242 drinkers; self-report). Add the DOM observational study in T2D as 'linked to', not 'causes'. Never give a 'safe amount'. Include the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas, and note that alcohol adds to dehydration and nausea. Ties into Thanksgiving.

candidates.topic: Pregnancy on tirzepatide: 232 pregnancies within 6 months of starting a GLP-1 (Adelaide, 1.6 million Australian women), the 'Ozempic baby' plot twist (NPR), and the large October study finding no detectable increase in pregnancy risks around conception
candidates.angle: A 20:00 funnel Short pointing to the Birth Control long-form. Weight loss may raise fertility. The tirzepatide label says it may reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase, so add a barrier method or ask about non-oral options. It isn't for use in pregnancy, so plan with your prescriber. No fear-mongering: the reassuring October data stays at its observational scope.
